section_1.title: Introduction: The Speed of Change (0:00-0:45)
section_1.content: Briefly recap the power rule for simple derivatives (x^n). Introduce the 'Dynamic Duo' rules required when functions interact: Product Rule (multiplication) and Chain Rule (nesting).
section_1.example: Visualize a robotic arm: The Product Rule tracks the arm's total reach (length × angle), while the Chain Rule tracks the motor speed inside the gear mechanism.

section_2.title: The Product Rule: The 'Teamwork' Formula (0:45-2:00)
section_2.content: Explain that when two functions multiply, f(x)g(x), the derivative isn't just the product of derivatives. It's 'derivative of the first times the second, plus the first times derivative of the second'. Use a graphic of two rectangles expanding.
section_2.example: A squirrel gathering nuts: If the number of squirrels (f) increases while the nuts per squirrel (g) increases, the total rate of collection follows the product rule.

section_3.title: The Chain Rule: The 'Nested' Layers (2:00-3:30)
section_3.content: Introduce the concept of composite functions f(g(x)). Use the 'Matryoshka Doll' (Russian nesting doll) analogy. The derivative is the 'outer derivative' times the 'inner derivative'.
section_3.example: A rocket's height: The altitude depends on fuel (inner), and the fuel consumption depends on time (outer). Derivative = (change in height/change in fuel) × (change in fuel/change in time).

section_4.title: Synthesis & Complex Application (3:30-4:30)
section_4.content: Demonstrate a hybrid problem requiring both rules. Show how the visual graph of a complex wave simplifies when broken into its procedural parts.
section_4.example: An animatronic character moving: Its arm extension is defined by f(g(x)) * h(x). Apply both rules step-by-step to calculate the instantaneous velocity.

section_5.title: Summary & Quick Check (4:30-5:00)
section_5.content: Summarize with a visual cheat sheet. Product Rule (Addition of terms), Chain Rule (Multiplication of factors).
section_5.example: Flashcard challenge: Quick identification of which rule applies to sin(x²) vs. x²sin(x).

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 2.5 + j * 0.8
                y = 2.0 - i * 0.8
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary & Quick Check", ["Cheat sheet: Key formula summary.", "Product rule uses addition.", "Chain rule uses multiplication."])
        
        # Animations
        # Create cheat sheet checklist
        checklist = VGroup(
            Text("Summary Checklist:", font_size=24, color=YELLOW),
            Text("1. Product Rule: (uv)' = u'v + uv'", font_size=20, color=WHITE),
            Text("2. Chain Rule: (f(g(x)))' = f'(g(x))g'(x)", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        ).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.4)
        
        self.place_in_area(checklist, 'A1', 'C6', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(checklist))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(Indicate(checklist[1], color=YELLOW))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(Indicate(checklist[2], color=YELLOW))
